info.name: IPPIS HRMS: all API tests
info.description:
Every API test for the IPPIS HRMS backend in one collection. Run the three parts in order; each part signs in again at its start, so a part can also be run on its own.

A. Roles and permissions: RBAC, route guards, separation of duties, account lifecycle and sign-in protection.
B. MDA scope, transfers and overview: each MDA sees only its own records, transfers move people and remove old access, the per-MDA overview, and the protected public registration flow.
C. Employee portal: invite, sign-in, profile, attendance, leave, payroll, tasks, documents, training and notifications.

BEFORE THE FIRST RUN
1. These migrations must be on the database the server uses (check with your notes; all are safe to re-run): database/rbac-migration.sql, the three database/employee-portal-migration*.sql files, database/organisation-links-migration.sql, database/employee-mda-migration.sql, database/transfer-migration.sql.
2. Start the backend with `pnpm dev` (baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:8000).
3. In Variables, set adminUsername and adminPassword (your super admin), and employeeId (a TEST employee record that has no portal account yet, for part C). testPassword is the password given to the test accounts; the default meets the password rules.

CODES AND LINKS
With `pnpm dev`, sign-in codes, invite links and reset links are printed in the backend terminal. Copy them into the variable a request's description names: otp, testOtp, hrOtp, inviteToken, resetToken. Requests that upload a file (EP110, EP115, EP117) need a file chosen in their Body tab.

WHAT IT WRITES
Test admin accounts, a custom role and test users are created and deleted again. Part B leaves two test employees ("Postman MdaA" and "Postman MdaB") with an attendance record and two transfers; part C gives the employeeId record a portal account and test requests. Use test records only.

The two verify-OTP requests need the code in `otp` / `testOtp`; with `pnpm dev` it is printed in the backend terminal. The requests create and then delete one test user and one custom role, and leave audit rows behind.

B. MDA scope, transfers and overview
item.description:
Tests for MDA isolation, transfers, the per-MDA overview and the protected public registration flow.

BEFORE YOU START
1. Run database/transfer-migration.sql on the database the server uses (the other two migrations are already on Neon).
2. Start the backend with `pnpm dev` (baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:8000).
3. Set the collection variables adminUsername and adminPassword (your super admin).

RUNNING
Run the folders in order. Two requests need a sign-in code:
- 02 needs `otp` (super admin), 10 needs `hrOtp` (the test HR officer). With `pnpm dev` each code is printed in the backend terminal ("[OTP Email] DEV MODE - OTP for ...").
Everything else fills its own variables. Requests 03-05 pick the first two active MDAs and a department in each; set mdaA / mdaB yourself to test with particular MDAs.

WHAT IT WRITES
This creates real records on the database behind the server:
- two test admin accounts (deleted again in folder 7),
- two test employees, "Postman MdaA" and "Postman MdaB" (emails postman.mda.a/b.<time>@example.com), one attendance record and two transfer records. These stay; there is no delete endpoint for employees.
A run is repeatable: each run uses new usernames and emails.

item.name: MD04 Choose MDA A and one of its departments

request.description: Uses mdaA if you set it, otherwise the first active MDA that has a department.

exec: const mda = wanted ? mdas.find(m => m.id === String(wanted)) : mdas.find(m => depts.some(d => String(d.company_id) === m.id));
const dept = mda && depts.find(d => String(d.company_id) === mda.id);
pm.test("MDA A has a department", () => pm.expect(dept).to.be.an("object"));
pm.collectionVariables.set("mdaA", mda.id); pm.collectionVariables.set("mdaAName", mda.name); pm.collectionVariables.set("deptA", dept.id);

request.description: Uses mdaB if you set it, otherwise the next active MDA that has a department.

exec: const mda = wanted ? mdas.find(m => m.id === String(wanted)) : mdas.find(m => m.id !== a && depts.some(d => String(d.company_id) === m.id));
const dept = mda && depts.find(d => String(d.company_id) === mda.id);
pm.test("MDA B has a department", () => pm.expect(dept).to.be.an("object"));
pm.collectionVariables.set("mdaB", mda.id); pm.collectionVariables.set("mdaBName", mda.name); pm.collectionVariables.set("deptB", dept.id);
